This re-maps the scalar field such that each voxel is treated as the lower-left corner of a cell [S4].

The claim states that the evidence re-maps the scalar field such that each voxel is treated as the lower-left corner of a cell. The source text explicitly states: 'By logically shifting the position of all scalars backward by half a unit of voxel width, we re-map our scalar field to cells.' It further explains that this approach allows the system to 'intersect with an 8-voxel... even though the data stored at each leaf node is actually a single scalar value,' and describes retrieving 'forward neighbors' to define the cell. This confirms that the single scalar value (voxel) is treated as the reference point (lower-left corner) for the 8-voxel cell.
